slides.title: How to read a certificate of analysis (COA)
slides.text: Swipe, here's what to look for 👉

slides.title: Mass spectrometry
slides.text: A COA should list a measured molecular mass next to a theoretical one. The words 'mass spec' alone, with no numbers, mean little.

slides.title: HPLC and an actual number
slides.text: Look for an HPLC result near 98% or higher, with a visible chromatogram. No chromatogram is a red flag.

slides.title: Matches the vial
slides.text: The lot number on the COA must match the vial's label. One generic COA reused across different batches is a red flag.

list: COA only available after you buy

slides.text: A COA describes one tested sample under a defined method. It doesn't confirm sterility, safety, or legality.
